on_screen_hook: Acid and glycolic acid is truly a trio that is one of
transcript: Acid and glycolic acid is truly a trio that is one of the best out there. But I'm a dermatologist and I'm telling you that not everyone actually needs all three of these. Azelaic acid is an anti inflammatory, so it's a great add on if you deal with underlying red, but if that's not you, you can go ahead and skip it because tretinoin alone can carry most of the work. And glycolic acid as an exfoliant once or twice a week is excellent, but if your skin tends to be sensitive, swap it for something like lactic or mandelic acid instead. You get the same exfoliating benefit, but they're much gentler. And the one rule that matters more than which ones you pick is to never stack all of these in the same routine. Rotate them, do not layer them. Comment below and I'll help clarify these in your routine.

creator: TheDailyDerm
title: Do NOT scrape off blackheads!
caption:
Scraping blackheads causes inflammation, enlarged pores, and hyperpigmentation. Instead, clear dead skin buildup and prevent new blackheads by consistently using Adapalene gel over a few weeks.

Brought to you by  @cerave .
transcript: If you have blackheads on your nose, you see these and you think you might just scrape it off yourself. Don't. You're actually making them worse. See, when dead skin cells and debris get mixed with your skin's oil, they clump together and start building up inside the pore. When that build-up reaches the surface and gets exposed to air, you get these dark, raised blackheads. So, when you grab one of these to scrape those spots away, you're doing more harm than good. You actually risk more skin inflammation, larger pore appearance, and a higher chance of hyper pigmentation. Instead, use a topical retinoid. It helps regulate how cells lining your pore behave, reducing blackhead formation. And the most important part, give it time. After several weeks of consistent use, then you'll start seeing results.
